proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Base change to a perfect closure k inside k': the restrictions R_i' to R_i are universal homeomorphisms as compositions of base changes of the universal homeomorphism U' to U (see the diagram in the restrict-groupoid-on-field lemma), so it suffices to prove the closedness of a'(R_1') in R_2'; assume k perfect. For perfect k the closure of the image is a groupoid scheme Z inside R_2 by the map-groupoids-on-perfect-field-image lemma, and the same lemma applied to id_{R_1} : R_1 to R_1 shows (R_2)_red is a groupoid scheme. Applying the open-image-is-closed lemma to the morphism a restricted to (R_2)_red, viewed as a morphism (R_2)_red to Z, gives that the image is closed in Z; it is also dense in Z by definition of Z as the closure, hence equals Z, so a(R_1) = Z is closed in R_2. (source lines 1822-1845)

standard_prerequisites.name: An open image of a morphism of groupoids over a field is closed (more-groupoids chapter, Lemma lemma-open-image-is-closed, canonical tag 04Q6; collected on this lane as L22517)
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to a restricted to (R_2)_red as a morphism (R_2)_red to Z: the image, being locally closed and dense in Z, is open in Z, hence closed in Z and equal to Z.

core_obligations: Reduction to perfect k: take a perfect closure k inside k'; the restrictions R_i' via U' = Spec(k') to Spec(k) have morphisms R_i' to R_i that are universal homeomorphisms, being compositions of base changes of the universal homeomorphism U' to U per the diagram in lemma-restrict-groupoid-on-field; universal homeomorphisms preserve the closedness of the image, so it suffices to prove a'(R_1') closed in R_2', and one may assume k perfect (proof lines 1823-1831). Perfect case: by lemma-map-groupoids-on-perfect-field-image the closure of the image is a groupoid scheme Z inside R_2, and the same lemma applied to id_{R_1} : R_1 to R_1 shows (R_2)_red is a groupoid scheme (proof lines 1834-1839). Conclusion: apply lemma-open-image-is-closed to the morphism a|_{(R_2)_red} : (R_2)_red to Z; the image is locally closed in R_2 by hypothesis, hence locally closed in Z, and dense in Z since Z is its closure; a dense locally closed subset is open in Z, so the lemma makes it closed in Z, whence it equals Z and a(R_1) = Z is closed in R_2 (proof lines 1840-1844).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to perfect k via the perfect closure and the universal homeomorphism property of the restrictions (proof lines 1823-1831).
Get the groupoid schemes Z and (R_2)_red from the map-groupoids-on-perfect-field-image lemma (proof lines 1834-1839).
Apply the open-image-is-closed lemma to the restriction over the reduced arrow scheme and conclude the equality with Z (proof lines 1840-1844).
